metadata.case_name: CHENG MAN CHI v. DR TAM KAI TAI CARL

injuries.description: Wrongful extraction of four upper incisors
source: the plaintiff’s claim against the defendant is for wrongful extraction of her four upper incisors and wrongful removal of a substantial portion of the bone above her upper incisors in the dental treatment given to her by the defendant.
On 14 June 2001 the extraction of the four upper incisors and the bone removal was performed. One to two mm of bone was trimmed off.

(90)(8) the plaintiff’s four upper canines were extracted on 14 June 2001. Quite apart from extracting the four upper incisors, the defendant had also filed off and removed some of her alveolar bone above the extracted incisors but without informing the plaintiff of his doing so;

injuries.description: Removal (filing off) of a substantial portion of the alveolar bone above the extracted upper incisors (osteotomy)

injuries.description: Major depressive disorder with mood congruous psychotic symptoms (psychiatric injury)
source: He diagnosed the plaintiff to suffer from a major depressive disorder with mood congruous psychotic symptoms.
By October 2004 she became depressed and weepy with difficulty sleeping. By the end of that year she began hearing voices asking her to die.

manifestations.description: both her upper canines were tilting slightly forward
implants turned out to be either mobile or mal-positioned
failing implant(s) with pus discharge: "pus was found extruding from the implant"
swelling in the distal region (as at last review on 21 July 2008)
weepiness, moodiness, insomnia, irritability, loss of interest, concentration and motivation for daily activities, poor appetite and weight loss
hearing voices asking her to die

treatments_received: extraction of the four upper incisors
osteotomy / filing off of alveolar bone above upper incisors
multiple dental bridges (including three made between mid August and September 2001)
total of 5 operations for installation of four implants (Dec 2001 - Aug 2004)
removal of implants under general anaesthetic on 18 April 2005
removal of titanium mesh tray and placement of four implants in anterior alveolar ridge under general anaesthetic on 1 August 2006
vestibuloplasty by palatal graft (27 March 2007) and second vestibuloplasty (29 June 2007)
emergency treatment for pus discharge from implant (7 May 2008)
endodontics for upper left canine on 8 July 2008
treatments_future: continued remedial treatment at PPDH to restore implants and replace temporary crowns with ceramic crowns
psychiatric treatment and psychotherapy (one year recommended by Dr Chan Chee Hung)

losses.description: Removal of four upper incisors and removal of a substantial portion of alveolar bone above the upper incisors

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Plaintiff felt people turned away from her, was afraid to look at her and wore a face mask to hide her face
She spent most of her time at home preoccupied with her dental problem and avoided public interaction
Plaintiff resigned abruptly from her job on 4 May 2004 as a result of her distress about her appearance and perceived rejection by colleagues

He diagnosed the plaintiff to suffer from a major depressive disorder with mood congruous psychotic symptoms. By October 2004 she became depressed and weepy with difficulty sleeping. By the end of that year she began hearing voices asking her to die.
